title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Neodymium (Nd, Z=60) is 144.242(3)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Neodymium (Nd, Z=60) as 144.242(3), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 60, symbol Nd, as Neodymium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Neodymium as 144.242(3). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Isotope rows in the same file: Nd-142 relative atomic mass 141.9077290(20), isotopic composition 0.27152(40); Nd-143 relative atomic mass 142.9098200(20), isotopic composition 0.12174(26); Nd-144 relative atomic mass 143.9100930(20), isotopic composition 0.23798(19); Nd-145 relative atomic mass 144.9125793(20), isotopic composition 0.08293(12); Nd-146 relative atomic mass 145.9131226(20), isotopic composition 0.17189(32); Nd-148 relative atomic mass 147.9168993(26), isotopic composition 0.05756(21); Nd-150 relative atomic mass 149.9209022(18), isotopic composition 0.05638(28). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
